review.summary: Reviewed the hash-routing implementation (new src/route.ts, tests/route.test.ts, and the App.tsx diff against base commit a9937c1) using only read-only tools; no repository files were changed. I traced every navigation call site (openProject, navigate, tab buttons, back link, repo "View projects" link) and confirmed all now go through goTo/applyRoute with no leftover direct setPage/setSelectedId/setTab calls, verified the malformed-route path (mount effect + hashchange listener) and the missing-project-id path (loadDetail 404 catch + stale-request guard) both surface the "global-error" banner on the board without pushing a new history entry (no redirect loop), and confirmed feedback/selectedItems/search/filter/conversationStage remain untouched by routing. route.test.ts (7 cases) exercises round-tripping, tab-slug defaulting, id encoding, and malformed detection soundly. The only functional issue found is low-severity (an inconsistency in malformed-detection strictness, not a violation of any stated acceptance criterion). Test-report caveat: the reported `npm run test` failure is confined to tests/workflow.test.ts (34 failures), all with the identical Windows long-path git error ("Filename too long" writing objects under this worktree's deep .data/tests path) — an environment limitation unrelated to routing; route.test.ts itself is not among the failures. I did not independently re-run npm scripts (read-only review stage) and did not exercise the app in a browser, so the manual click-through/back-forward/reload checks described in the plan are unverified by me, though the code paths for them look correct on inspection.

items.title: Inconsistent malformed detection for trailing extra path segments
items.description: For repositories/skills/settings routes, any extra trailing segment (e.g. `#/repositories/extra`) is flagged malformed (route.ts:27). For project routes, extra segments beyond id/tab (e.g. `#/project/abc123/Overview/junk`) are silently ignored — `rest[2]`, `rest[3]`, etc. are never inspected (route.ts:39-41), so the route is accepted as valid with tab defaulted/matched from rest[1]. This doesn't violate any acceptance criterion (a usable route is still produced) but is an inconsistency in how strictly malformed input is detected across route kinds; a user pasting a mistyped project link with trailing garbage gets silently normalized while the equivalent static-page case gets an error banner. Low-risk cosmetic/consistency nit, not a functional defect.
